children: The Chinese yuan's appreciation against the dollar has slowed in recent months and this more gradual pace is likely to continue, Commerzbank's Volkmar Baur says in a note. "Given weak domestic demand, the Chinese economy remains reliant on a robust contribution from net exports," he says. As long as the dollar remains strong on a trade-weighted basis, Chinese policymakers are unlikely to allow a faster appreciation of the yuan as this would result in excessive strengthening against other currencies, he says. The dollar falls 0.1% to 6.6806 yuan after earlier reaching a four-year low of 6.6805, according to LSEG. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
